question: A 65-year-old African-American man presents to your office with dysphagia. He reports that he has found it progressively more difficult to swallow food over the past year. At the time of presentation, he is able to eat only soup. Social history is significant for asbestos exposure, multiple daily drinks of hard alcohol, and a 70 pack-year smoking history. What would you most expect to see on an esophageal biopsy of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Dysphagia -> difficulty swallowing -> esophageal biopsy -> findings CHAIN: Asbestos exposure, alcohol consumption, smoking history -> increased risk of esophageal pathology -> esophageal biopsy findings CHAIN: Dysphagia + significant social history -> esophageal biopsy -> abnormal findings CHAIN: Dysphagia + difficulty swallowing + significant social history -> esophageal biopsy -> abnormal histopathology CHAIN: Dysphagia + difficulty swallowing + asbestos exposure + alcohol consumption + smoking history -> esophageal biopsy -> abnormal histopathology -> 90%
analysis: Given the patient's history of asbestos exposure, heavy alcohol consumption, and smoking, the most likely finding on esophageal biopsy would be glandular metaplasia, which is associated with Barrett's esophagus and an increased risk of esophageal adenocarcinoma.
